name: FamilyWatchingSports

custom.system_prompt: The Brennan family — Siobhan, Patrick, and Cillian — are watching a live football or rugby match together. Patrick is the resident expert for anything before 2010; Cillian knows the current players and statistics; Siobhan is half-watching. A factual disagreement between Patrick and Cillian about a player's record or career history cannot be resolved between them. Sigma is addressed once to settle it.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Comfortable family living room in the evening, live football or rugby on television, stadium crowd noise, commentary audible in the background, occasional excited reaction from the commentator, comfortable domestic sounds.

initial_prompt: Generate a lively, warm family conversation between Siobhan, Patrick, and Cillian watching a live football or rugby match. Patrick is the 1990s expert — he knows the classic players, the legendary seasons, the old records. Cillian knows current players, current statistics, and recent seasons. Siobhan is half-watching but occasionally engages or asks a question that complicates things. A question comes up about a specific player's career record — how many caps, goals, or a specific milestone — that spans the gap between what Patrick knows (old data) and what Cillian knows (recent data). They disagree and cannot resolve it. Cillian reaches for his phone; Patrick tells him to put it down. The game continues with reactions and personal topics in between. The question returns at a significant game moment. Eventually Siobhan addresses Sigma to settle it — she finds the debate tiresome and wants to watch the match. Sigma gives the answer in one sentence. The family reacts and returns to the game. Sigma is not addressed again.

user1.name: Siobhan
user1.tts_prompt: Warm, dry, half-watching, occasionally decisive when the debate goes on too long

user2.name: Patrick
user2.tts_prompt: Engaged with the match, confident about old-school knowledge, direct

user3.name: Cillian
user3.tts_prompt: Energetic, current-stats confident, Cork teenage voice

variations.context: An Irish family watching a live football or rugby match. A generational knowledge gap about a player's career record is settled by Sigma when Siobhan tires of the debate.

setting.mood: Patrick and Cillian are engaged with the match; Siobhan is present but half-distracted. The debate is good-natured but persistent.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Patrick has historical authority — he watched these teams in the 1990s and knows the old records. Cillian has current authority — he follows the Premier League or Six Nations closely and knows recent stats. Neither can bridge the gap. Siobhan uses Sigma as a practical tool to end the argument and watch the match.
setting.background: The match is well underway — second half or second set. The family has been watching since the start.
setting.conversation_style: Match reactions interspersed with the generational debate and family conversation.

scenario_template.topic: They react to the current state of the match. Patrick comments on the formation or a player's position; Cillian has an opinion about recent form; Siobhan asks a question.

A player does something notable. Patrick compares him to a legend from decades ago or references a record he thinks the player is close to. Cillian has a different number. They disagree about whether the record stands.
scenario_template.note: Non-trigger moment. Cillian reaches for phone; Patrick stops him. No Sigma.

scenario_template.topic: Siobhan points out that something just happened on the pitch that they both missed because of the argument. Brief match focus.
A break in play — halftime, injury, or replay. A family topic comes up: the weekend, Cillian's football club, Patrick's extension, Siobhan's school.
A significant moment: a goal, a try, a near-miss, a controversial call. They react.
The player has another notable involvement. Patrick's original claim comes back up. Cillian has now looked at the question from a different angle. They are stuck in the same place.
Siobhan, tired of the debate, addresses Sigma and asks for the specific statistic. She frames it practically — she wants to watch the match.
scenario_template.note: Exactly one request and one response. Sigma gives the number in one sentence.
Cillian insists the player has a different nickname this season; Patrick disagrees. Siobhan adds a humorous twist.
Patrick recalls attending a record-breaking game in the 90s; Cillian skeptically questions whether any game could top recent events.

scenario_template.topic: Comment on a neighbor dropping by earlier
scenario_template.note: Siobhan mentions seeing a neighbor earlier who commented on the match; Patrick adds his two cents about the neighbor's football opinions.

scenario_template.topic: Patrick recalls a funny story about Cillian
scenario_template.note: Patrick tells an embarrassing but funny story about Cillian's younger football days; Cillian feigns annoyance but laughs.

scenario_template.topic: Brief discussion on snacks or drinks
scenario_template.note: Siobhan offers to grab more snacks or drinks; Cillian makes a specific request.
Cillian criticizes a commentator's analysis; Patrick agrees, comparing them unfavorably with commentators from his youth.
Cillian comments on the current team's strategy compared to last season's; Siobhan asks a clarifying question, and Patrick gives historical context.

scenario_template.topic: Siobhan talks about a work project
scenario_template.note: During a lull in the game, Siobhan mentions a challenging new project at work; Patrick shows interest and asks for details.

scenario_template.topic: They all react: who was right, Patrick's acceptance or mild surprise, Cillian's satisfaction or mild outrage, Siobhan telling them both to watch the match.

assistant_trigger_design.latent_need: A generational knowledge gap prevents the family from confirming a specific player record that spans the 1990s and the present.
assistant_trigger_design.early_non_trigger: Cillian's phone attempt is the early non-trigger — stopped by Patrick. The debate then continues for pleasure.
activation_evidence: The player has another notable moment that brings the question back.
Both Patrick and Cillian have committed to specific numbers they cannot verify.
Neither can bridge the gap between old and recent data.
Siobhan addresses Sigma to end the debate.
assistant_trigger_design.desired_response: The specific career statistic in one sentence.
undesired_behavior: Sigma responding to Cillian's first phone reach.
Sigma commenting on the match in progress.

possible_sigma_queries: Sigma, how many caps does he have?
Sigma, how many international goals does he have?
Sigma, how many Premier League goals has he scored?
Sigma, how many Six Nations tries does he have?
Sigma, is he the all-time leading scorer for Ireland?
possible_sigma_answers: He has 103 international caps, the most for any outfield player in this squad.
He has scored 68 international goals across all competitions.
He has 187 Premier League goals, which puts him sixth all-time.
He has 32 Six Nations tries — the record for Ireland.
Yes, he became the all-time leading scorer for Ireland in March of this year.

family_topics: Cillian's club football and his coach
Patrick's house extension and when it will be done
Siobhan's school and a particular class she's dealing with
Whether they will go to a live match at some point
A relative who supports a different team
match_reactions: A controversial offside call Patrick disagrees with
A chance missed that Patrick says they will regret
A defensive error Siobhan notices before the others
The halftime score and whether it is fair
realism_devices: Patrick's number is from twenty years ago and has been broken since.
Cillian's number is from this season and does not include older records.
Siobhan notices a missed chance while they are arguing.
Cillian tries to reach for his phone a second time with greater stealth.
Patrick quotes his 1990s figure with the authority of someone who was there.

user1.name: Siobhan
user1.role: Mother. Half-watching but engaged enough to notice missed plot points. Uses Sigma when the debate between Patrick and Cillian goes on too long.

user2.name: Patrick
user2.role: Father. 1990s sports expert. Confident about historical records. Stopped Cillian's phone attempt. Accepts Sigma as the household device.

user3.name: Cillian
user3.role: Teenage son. Current-stats expert. Reaches for phone multiple times. Genuinely wants to know the answer — uses Sigma naturally.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Responds exactly once when Siobhan addresses it. Gives the specific statistic in one sentence. Does not comment on the match or the debate.

conversation_structure: Three-way family conversation with clear generational knowledge roles.
Cillian's phone attempt is the early non-trigger — stopped by Patrick.
The generational knowledge gap must create a genuine impasse before Sigma is used.
Siobhan addresses Sigma as a practical decision, not a technological one.
The Sigma exchange occupies exactly two turns.
assistant_behavior: Sigma responds exactly once when Siobhan addresses it.
Sigma gives the specific career statistic in one sentence.
Sigma does not comment on the match or on the generational debate.
Sigma remains silent after its single answer.
quality_checks: Patrick and Cillian must both contribute substantively to the debate.
The generational gap must be clearly established before the Sigma request.
At least one significant match moment should interrupt the debate.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
